what_each_new_part_touches: Yellow box 1: the black turntable top is pressed onto the grey base ring. Yellow box 2: four blue pins go into the blocks on the top ring. The finished turntable is lowered onto the middle of the undercarriage (arrow) and the four grey pins (green arrows, two from each side) are pushed in through the base ring to lock it.
where_everything_is_after: the turntable sits on the middle of the undercarriage with its base locked by the four grey pins; the top ring can turn on it

why.problem_solved: Gives the machine a ring that lets the whole upper body swing round on the tracks.
why.why_these_parts: A slewing ring (grey base + black top) is the Technic version of a real excavator's swing bearing; the four long pins already waiting in the frame lock the base without extra parts.
why.sets_up_for_later: Everything from step 18 onward that is part of the upper body is built on the black top ring.

review_note: The four pins that lock the base are the grey pins of step 15. Which of the base's six side holes (hole1-3 left, hole4-6 right) each one takes is an estimate (two per side). The blue pins go into the top ring's blocks; their exact holes are not named.
